# Do Code That Matters
> Personal blog by Spencer Kittleson — software development, local LLMs, 3D printing, IoT, and maker projects. All content is original first-hand writing with working code.

## About the author
- [Spencer Kittleson](https://docodethatmatters.com/about/): Software engineer. GitHub: https://github.com/skittleson

## Posts
- [Sony A6000 and A6400 Research: Hacks, Mods and Community Resources](https://docodethatmatters.com/sony-a6000-a6400-research/) (2026-08-29): Deep-dive reference on hacking, modding, and community resources for the Sony A6000 (ILCE-6000) and A6400 (ILCE-6400) — OpenMemories-Tweak, PMCA-RE firmware dumping, clean HDMI/webcam hacks, IR & full-spectrum conversions, power/battery mods, S-Log video, timelapse, and the Sony PlayMemories app archive.
- [How I Run Local LLMs for Coding (and Why the Quant Matters)](https://docodethatmatters.com/running-local-llms-for-coding/) (2026-08-19): How I run a coding LLM locally on a single RTX 3090 Ti — the model journey from Claude-distilled to a dense 27B coder, why MoE beat dense for speed, why I stayed on llama.cpp over vLLM on Ampere, and the quant type and sampler flag that quietly bit me.
- [I scanned the BLE devices around my house - they are sharing everything](https://docodethatmatters.com/i-scanned-the-ble-devices-around-my-house/) (2026-06-17): An inspired project from DEFCON 2024 of the Wall of Sheep with ble devices
- [The Infinite Echo: a State-Mirror Bug That Applies the Effect but Not the Dedup Key](https://docodethatmatters.com/the-infinite-echo-state-mirror-bug/) (2026-06-01): A state-mirror rule that updates the relay but never the dedup key guarantees an infinite echo, the same failure shape as replication storms and webhook retry loops. I found it live in two MQTT-linked light switches.
- [I tried to do OAuth token exchange with Authentik. Here is the security tradeoff nobody mentions.](https://docodethatmatters.com/oauth-token-exchange-sso-demo/) (2026-03-23): Authentik does not support RFC 8693 token exchange. The workaround works, but it shifts a security assumption most people never notice. Here is what I found and how it compares to Keycloak.
- [Building a Custom HTTP Proxy in Rust for Mixed-OS Workflows](https://docodethatmatters.com/building-custom-http-proxy-rust-mixed-os-workflows/) (2026-03-16): How I built a Rust-powered transparent HTTP(S) proxy to seamlessly route my Linux traffic through a Windows work machine, with PopOS setup, Docker config, and Chromium proxy tips.
- [Building a Custom HTTP Proxy in Rust for Mixed-OS Workflows](https://docodethatmatters.com/building-custom-http-proxy-rust-mixed-os-workflows/) (2026-03-15): I built a Rust proxy to keep my traffic private and give me remote access to home devices. It's lightweight, no-app, works on any device that can point to a proxy.
- [Tethered Raspberry Pi for Modern Camera Functionality](https://docodethatmatters.com/sony-camera-part3/) (2024-06-28): How I built a laptop-free tethered camera setup on a Raspberry Pi, with a custom Bluetooth binary protocol, server-side JPEG compression, and zero-config LAN browsing.
- [My Emails Are Out Of Control](https://docodethatmatters.com/emails_out_of_control/) (2024-06-25): My emails are out of control. In order to take some of it back, i decided to write some python scripts to help out.
- [Part 2 of Hacking my Sony A6000 Camera](https://docodethatmatters.com/hacking-sony-a6000-more/) (2024-05-14): Second part of hacking a Sony A6000 series camera and upgrading data transfer capabilities. This one is about free apps with time lapse, ftp uploader, and building usb-c power adapter for on the go.
- [Hacking my Sony A6000 Camera Adding Modern Features](https://docodethatmatters.com/hacking-sony-a6000-for-modernization/) (2023-07-17): Discover how to modernize your Sony A6000 camera by upgrading its data transfer capabilities and post process images for super high resolution. Join the journey of enhancing your camera's features in this comprehensive blog post.
- [Linux Wifi Hotspot with PiHole](https://docodethatmatters.com/linux-wifi-hotspot-usb3/) (2022-09-29): Build a wifi hotspot using hostapd via create_ap project and pihole.
- [Effective Onboarding for New Engineers](https://docodethatmatters.com/onboarding-devs/) (2022-07-05): Learn an effective onboarding strategy for new engineers on a project. Streamline the transition and boost productivity with our structured approach.
- [Parametric Belt Driven 3D Printed Spur Gear for Electric Skateboards](https://docodethatmatters.com/skateboard-gear/) (2022-06-20): Update on using a parametric 3D printed gear for my DIY electric skateboard after 100+ hours of riding.
- [Top 5 Nuget Packages](https://docodethatmatters.com/top-nuget-packages/) (2022-03-07): Top nuget packages in dotnet including fluent validation, counting lines, dependency injection, retry logic, and testing/mocking libraries.
- [Automate Cleaning of Air Conditioner Condensate Drain Line](https://docodethatmatters.com/automate-cleaning-of-air-conditioner-condensate-drain-line/) (2021-12-31): Flash a smart wifi dual water pump to automate cleaning the air conditioner line. A common home maintenance task that is easily forgotten to do each month.
- [Common Apps for Devs over Chocolatey](https://docodethatmatters.com/chocolately-for-devs/) (2021-10-03): Automate software install for a software engineer on Windows
- [Local First, Cloud Assisted ☁ MultiSensor](https://docodethatmatters.com/neosiren-tasmota-local-first-cloud-assisted-iot/) (2021-04-27): Guide for flashing a temperature and humidity multisensor with Tasmota for local network first setup.
- [A simple water sprinkler system, for makers!](https://docodethatmatters.com/automate-sprinkler-with-tasmota/) (2020-11-02): Setup a water sprinkler using open source hardware/software to trigger based on special conditions like time (including sunrise/sunset), humidity, and perhaps temperature.
- [Duplicator i3 3d printer upgrade](https://docodethatmatters.com/3dprinter-duplicator-i3-upgrade/) (2020-06-01): Upgrades for to Duplicator i3 and replacing with a MKS Gen 1.4 Board.
- [Power Switch Monitor with an Arduino device](https://docodethatmatters.com/power-switch-monitor/) (2020-06-01): Automate smart devices using an existing light switch and power switch monitor with an Arduino compatible device with wifi.
- [Save JSON Objects to AWS S3 with Google Recaptcha](https://docodethatmatters.com/json-to-s3-with-google-recaptcha/) (2019-10-19): Save JSON objects to AWS S3 using Google Recaptcha in a AWS Lambda function.
- [Research on Bluetooth Proximity](https://docodethatmatters.com/research-bluetooth-proximity/) (2019-10-19): Research on bluetooth proximity using open tools such as hcitool, l2ping, and hcidump
- [Software Engineering Lessons](https://docodethatmatters.com/software-engineering-lessons/) (2018-10-23): In the field notes and lessons learned as a software engineer.
- [Yet Another Garage Door Opener](https://docodethatmatters.com/yet-another-garage-door-opener/) (2018-05-11): Just another garage door opener using a raspberry pi
- [ASP.NET XSS protection](https://docodethatmatters.com/asp-net-xss-protection/) (2017-09-06): "Securing an ASP.NET WebApi for PCI application tests is no trivial matter. It can take weeks of planning and the app to be analyzed. After reviewing OWASP and other related XSS sites, the web.config was the first to be updated to prevent against attacks (MIIM & XSS)."
- [Raspberry Pi Bluetooth Proximity Detector - A Simple Guide](https://docodethatmatters.com/raspberry-pi-bluetooth-proximity/) (2017-05-26): Build a Bluetooth proximity detector using Raspberry Pi. Tutorial shows how to detect nearby Bluetooth devices without pairing.
